statement: This file says what a PASS establishes and what it does not. Every 'does not' is either demonstrated by a fixture pair that both verify, or already declared by the verifier itself; nothing here is an opinion about our own product.

guarantees.says: The package bytes are the bytes the signer signed, under a key the reader can pin out of band.
guarantees.how: Ed25519 seal over identity + manifest + lifecycle; open mode reads the key out of the package, --pubkey pins it.

guarantees.says: Evidence entries have not changed since the package was sealed.
guarantees.how: Per-entry SHA-256 plus a Merkle root recomputed from the shipped files.

guarantees.says: The declared file set is the file set: no undeclared file sits beside it.
guarantees.how: Package layout check; notes are listed, --strict turns notes into failures.

guarantees.says: Identity fields agree with each other and with the lifecycle, and every event actor is an authorised principal.
guarantees.how: Cross-field identity consistency, state machine, actor authorisation.

guarantees.says: The checkpoint matches the contents, so truncation is caught; rollback is caught only against a head observed outside the package.
guarantees.how: S8 recomputes the checkpoint; S9 compares it to --expect-head or a state file.

guarantees.says: When an RFC 3161 token is shipped, it verifies offline against the CA bundle shipped beside it.
guarantees.how: Signature, message imprint and certificate chain checked without a network.

guarantees.says: Six closure components were declared, each with a digest.
guarantees.how: Declaration check only - see N3 for what that does not mean.

non_guarantees.statement: It does not establish that the signer is the legal entity named in the package.
non_guarantees.why: Verification binds a package to a key. The key is a test seed anyone can re-use; nothing in the format links a key to a registry, a domain, or a person.

evidence.differs_by: the owner field: 'alice' against 'acme-medical-devices-gmbh', same signing key

non_guarantees.statement: It does not establish that the evidence set is complete.
non_guarantees.why: It can prove an entry was not altered after sealing. It cannot say whether an entry was never taken, because there is nothing to compare the set against. The nine-word version: absence is not evidence of absence.

evidence.differs_by: two evidence entries against three, both sealed after the fact

non_guarantees.statement: It does not compare the files shipped beside a closure digest against that digest.
non_guarantees.why: S10 checks that six components were declared with digests. The digests are written once, over whatever was on disk at seal time, and files under closure/ sit outside the evidence root, so nothing re-reads them. Replace a closure file after sealing and the declared digest points at bytes that are no longer there - the package still verifies. Nor is the content judged: a one-line file named model_weights.txt satisfies the declaration either way.

evidence.differs_by: the closure file body after sealing - one still hashes to the declared digest, one does not
evidence.observed: both PASS; S10 detail says 'declaration only, contents are not verified'

non_guarantees.statement: It does not establish when the package existed unless an external token is present.
non_guarantees.why: A timestamp inside the package is written by whoever built it. Only an RFC 3161 or OTS anchor, checked against a source the reader trusts, moves the claim from 'the author says' to 'a third party says'.

non_guarantees.statement: It does not evaluate the agent's behaviour.
non_guarantees.why: The verifier answers whether a record is intact and internally consistent. Whether the recorded action was correct, safe, or compliant is a different question, judged by a different instrument.

non_guarantees.statement: It does not verify the signatures on lifecycle events.
non_guarantees.why: Event signatures are not ratified in the format and the verifier does not check them; a lifecycle chain is checked for order and actors, not for per-event attestation.

industries.name: Medical device QMS and cybersecurity file
industries.reason: The reviewer wants records that survive ten years, verify without a vendor online, and show exactly what was and was not covered. That is the shape of this format, and the FDA/MDR documents ask for retained, reproducible evidence rather than a live service.

industries.name: Audit, legal and settlement records
industries.reason: Low volume, high value, adversarial later reading: the reader needs to attack the record, not trust a dashboard.

industries.name: Supply-chain handoff between parties
industries.reason: An offline package plus an external time anchor covers the handoff; the weak part is entity identity (N1), which the parties have to solve contractually.

industries.name: Consumer content provenance (images, video, audio)
industries.reason: Out of scope by design: this format carries no asset-to-manifest hard binding, no soft binding, and no ingestion at capture time.

industries.name: High-volume agent telemetry
industries.reason: Cost structure: per-record sealing, a Merkle tree, a receipt chain and an anchor is priced for records someone will litigate over, not for a million rows a day.
industries.peer_that_covers_it: sigstore (Rekor) signs at volume; no anchoring scheme is priced per million rows

industries.name: Regulatory certification or accreditation
industries.reason: No accreditation, no notified body, no scheme ownership. Saying a product 'complies with MDR' or 'satisfies FDA guidance' on the strength of a passing verifier would be an overclaim, and this repository does not make it.
industries.peer_that_covers_it: notified bodies under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 Annex II and FDA premarket review - assessment activities, not formats
